questions.question: In OR Modelling, which description defines a directed network?
options: A network whose edges each have a specified orientation
A network whose edges each carry a numerical value
A network whose vertices are numbered in a fixed order
A network in which each edge may be used in both directions

questions.question: A directed network contains the edge $i\to j$. What does this edge imply about travel from $j$ to $i$?
options: It is allowed, since $i\to j$ joins the pair $i$ and $j$
Nothing; travel from $j$ to $i$ needs an edge $j\to i$
It is forbidden, as $j\to i$ cannot also be an edge
It is allowed whenever $i\to j$ carries no numerical value

questions.question: In which situation should the connection between $i$ and $j$ be modelled as a directed edge?
options: Water can run from tank $i$ to tank $j$ but never back
Towns $i$ and $j$ share a two-way road of length 7
Computers $i$ and $j$ exchange messages over one cable
Town $i$ is larger than town $j$, and a road joins them

questions.question: In a directed network for the transport of goods, vertex $v$ has the edges $u\to v$ and $v\to w$. How do these two edges differ at $v$?
options: They play the same role at $v$, as both have $v$ as an end
$u\to v$ brings goods into $v$; $v\to w$ carries goods out of $v$
$u\to v$ carries goods out of $v$, because it is listed first
Their roles at $v$ depend on their values, not on their directions

questions.question: A town is modelled as a directed network with junctions as vertices. How should a two-way street between junctions $i$ and $j$ be represented?
options: By the single edge $i\to j$, which also covers $j$ to $i$
By one edge between $i$ and $j$ with no orientation
By two edges, $i\to j$ and $j\to i$, one per direction
By the single edge $i\to j$ with its value doubled

questions.question: Reservoir $R$ feeds tanks $T_1$ and $T_2$ through pipes, and a third pipe lets water run from $T_1$ into $T_2$; water never runs back in any pipe. Which edge set models the pipes?
Tasks are the vertices of a directed network, and each edge records which of two tasks must come first. Task $P$ must be completed before task $Q$ starts. Which edge records this?
options: $Q\to P$, pointing from $Q$ to the task it waits for
Both $P\to Q$ and $Q\to P$, as the two tasks are linked
$P\to Q$, pointing from the earlier task to the later one
$P\to Q$, but only if $Q$ starts as soon as $P$ ends

questions.question: A directed network has the edges $A\to C$, $B\to C$, $C\to D$, $C\to E$ and $E\to C$. How many of these edges leave vertex $C$?
options: 5, all edges with an end at $C$
3, namely $A\to C$, $B\to C$, $E\to C$
1, as $C\to E$ and $E\to C$ cancel out
2, namely $C\to D$ and $C\to E$

questions.question: A town has only the one-way streets $X\to Y$, $Y\to Z$ and $Z\to X$, each usable only in its direction. A driver at $Y$ wants to reach $X$. Which way of driving is allowed?
options: Directly from $Y$ to $X$ along $X\to Y$
None; no street leads from $Y$ to $X$
$Y\to Z$, $Z\to Y$, then $Y\to X$
First $Y\to Z$, and after that $Z\to X$

questions.question: A one-way bridge from $P$ to $Q$ charges a toll of 3 euros and is modelled as the edge $P\to Q$ with value 3. What does this model say about crossing this bridge from $Q$ to $P$?
options: It costs 3 euros, the same toll as from $P$
It costs $-3$ euros, as the reverse way is negative
It is not possible; $P\to Q$ allows only $P$ to $Q$
It is free, since the toll is charged only from $P$

questions.question: A road between junctions $i$ and $j$ can be driven both ways, but uphill from $i$ to $j$ takes 9 minutes and downhill from $j$ to $i$ takes 5. How should a directed network with travel times represent it?
options: Edge $i\to j$ with value 9 and edge $j\to i$ with value 5
One edge $i\to j$ with value 7, the average of both times
Edges $i\to j$ and $j\to i$, both with value 9, the slower time
One edge $i\to j$ with value 9, the downhill trip being implied

questions.question: In a directed network a route uses edges one after another, each in its direction. Vertex $s$ has the edges $s\to a$ and $s\to b$, and no edge ends at $s$. Which statement about $s$ is correct?
options: Routes can arrive at $s$ by using $s\to a$ in reverse
Vertex $s$ is not allowed, as each vertex needs an incoming edge
Routes can start at $s$, but no route can arrive at $s$
No route can start at $s$, since it has no incoming edge

questions.question: A directed network should let every connection be used in both directions with the same value. Which condition on its edges is necessary and sufficient for this?
options: Each edge $i\to j$ has a reverse $j\to i$ of equal value
The network has an even number of edges in total
Every vertex has at least one incoming and one outgoing edge
Each edge $i\to j$ has a reverse $j\to i$ of any value

questions.question: A directed network has vertices $A,B,C$ and edges $A\to B$ and $B\to C$; a route uses edges one after another, each in its direction. Which single added edge lets every vertex reach every other vertex by a route?
options: $B\to A$
$A\to C$
$C\to B$
$C\to A$

questions.question: Four tasks are done one at a time, and an edge $X\to Y$ means task $X$ must be finished before task $Y$ starts. The edges are $P\to Q$, $P\to R$, $Q\to S$ and $R\to S$. Which order respects all edges?

A directed network on $A,B,C$ is given by a table whose entry in row $i$, column $j$ is 1 if the edge $i\to j$ exists and 0 if not. The off-diagonal entries are $(A,B)=1$, $(B,A)=1$, $(B,C)=1$, $(C,B)=0$, $(C,A)=1$, $(A,C)=0$. Which description is correct?
options: 3 edges, as $A\to B$ and $B\to A$ count as one edge
6 edges, one for each of the six listed table entries
4 edges; $A$ and $C$ are joined both ways
4 edges; only $A$ and $B$ are joined both ways

questions.question: In a directed network a route uses edges one after another, each in its direction. Vertex $X$ can be reached from vertex $W$ by a route. Does it follow that $W$ can be reached from $X$?
options: Yes; the edges of the route can be used backwards from $X$ to $W$
Yes, provided every edge on the route from $W$ to $X$ has a value
No; in a directed network $W$ can never be reached from $X$
No; with only the edge $W\to X$, no route leads from $X$ to $W$

questions.question: Tasks are vertices, and an edge $X\to Y$ means task $X$ must be finished before task $Y$ starts. The precedence data contain $P\to Q$, $Q\to R$ and $R\to P$. What does this say about the data?
options: They are consistent; the tasks can be done in the order $P$, $Q$, $R$
They are contradictory, since $P$ would have to precede itself
They are consistent; the three tasks just run at the same time
They are consistent, as each task has one incoming and one outgoing edge

questions.question: A town has only the one-way streets $A\to B$, $C\to B$ and $C\to D$, each usable only in its direction, and a route uses streets one after another. Is there a route from $A$ to $D$?
options: No; from $A$ only $B$ is reached, and no street leaves $B$
Yes: $A\to B$, then $C\to B$ backwards to $C$, then $C\to D$
Yes, since $A$ and $D$ are linked once directions are ignored
Yes: $A\to B$, and then a direct street from $B$ to $D$

questions.question: A directed network on $A,B,C,D$ has at every vertex at least one edge leaving and one edge entering; a route uses edges one after another, each in its direction. Which network shows that this does not ensure that every vertex can reach every other?
options: $A\to B$, $B\to C$, $C\to D$, $D\to A$
$A\to B$, $B\to A$, $C\to D$, $D\to C$
$A\to B$, $B\to C$, $C\to D$
$A\to B$, $B\to A$, $B\to C$, $C\to D$, $D\to B$
